مرکز پژوهشی فیزیک انرژی بالا (RCHEP) در: The Research Center for High Energy Physics (RCHEP) at Sharif University of Technology leads cutting-edge theoretical and experimental research in particle physics, quantum field theory, cosmology, string theory, and CERN collaborations.
مرکز روی پرسش‌های ژرف فیزیک بنیادین متمر: The center focuses on profound questions in fundamental physics, from subatomic scales to the largest cosmic structures.
تحقیقات در مرکز فیزیک انرژی بالا در سه ش: Research at RCHEP is organized across three main pillars: theoretical, experimental, and cosmological physics.

مرکز پژوهشی فیزیک انرژی بالا در زمستان س: The Research Center for High Energy Physics was founded in the winter of 2023 at Sharif University of Technology with the goal of advancing fundamental high-energy physics research in Iran, and its charter was officially approved.
ایده تأسیس این مرکز با پیشنهاد و پشتیبان: The establishment of this center originated from the proposal and support of Prof. Cumrun Vafa (renowned string theorist and Harvard professor). The initial funding was generously provided from the Mustafa Prize in science and technology awarded to him. The Mustafa Prize is a biennial international award granted to leading Muslim scientists worldwide.
دکتر شاهین روحانی | استاد دانشکده فیزیک: Prof. Shahin Rouhani | Professor of Physics & Director of RCHEP
هدف ما در این مرکز، ایجاد محیطی پویا و ا: Our goal is to foster a vibrant and inspiring academic environment for fundamental physics at the frontiers of science, train the next generation of researchers, and cultivate global collaborations with premier research institutions such as CERN. RCHEP serves as a bridge connecting theoretical concepts and experiments to address the deepest questions of our universe.
پژوهش در مسائل به‌روز فیزیک ذرات نظری و: Investigating modern problems in theoretical and experimental particle physics, string theory, and quantum gravity.

مشارکت فعال در آزمایشگاه‌های بین‌المللی: Active participation in leading international experiments, including the CMS detector at CERN.
